text: Berbeo is a town and municipality located in the Lengupá Province of the Colombian department of Boyacá. Its urban centre lies at an altitude of 1,350 metres (4,430 ft) within the Eastern Ranges of the Colombian Andes. The municipality shares borders with San Eduardo to the east, Zetaquirá and Miraflores to the west, Zetaquirá to the north, and Miraflores and Páez to the south. Previously known as San Fernando de Aguablanca and Legupá, Berbeo has been officially named after Juan Francisco Berbeo since 1913. Before the Spanish conquest, the region was inhabited by the indigenous Muisca people, and petroglyphs have been found in the area. Modern Berbeo was established on April 23, 1743, by Jesuits. The primary economic activity in Berbeo is agriculture, with coffee and chonto tomatoes being the main agricultural products.
